protocol: Two reviewers labelled independently, then reconciled. A defect is labelled only if a maintainer would plausibly request a change for it. Line = the line a review comment should attach to; matching tolerance is +/-3 lines.
known_limits: Two entries (fetcher.py:36, cache.py:27) are semantic defects that no pattern rule can detect. They are kept in the ground truth on purpose, so recall reflects what the reviewer actually misses instead of being defined by what the rules can find.

labels.note: mutable default argument seen=[] is shared across all calls
time.sleep blocks the event loop inside a coroutine
blocking requests.get inside a coroutine serialises the fan-out
bare except hides every error including KeyboardInterrupt
parse_rule evaluates user input and has no test at all
eval on a user-supplied expression is arbitrary code execution
SEMANTIC: summarise indexes payloads[0] and raises IndexError on an empty list
lock acquired without try/finally; an exception in _evict_if_needed deadlocks every other thread
assert used for runtime invariant is removed under python -O
SEMANTIC: sorted(self._store)[0] evicts the lexicographically smallest key, not the oldest entry, so the cache evicts the wrong item
file opened without a context manager leaks the handle when write raises
print in library code should be logging
string-built command with shell=True allows shell injection via destination
